description: Cross-binding conformance for esm-libraries-spec §4.7.1 — what an `operator_compose` entry MERGED, and which spelling of a bare-name match SURVIVES. Step 5 used to make silence normative: an entry that merged everything and one that merged nothing produced the same observable outcome, so a document could integrate a private decoupled operator while the mechanism got no contribution at all, and the only evidence was a state count one too high. Three things are pinned here and they are DISTINCT. (1) An entry that merges NOTHING is `operator_compose_no_merge`, a hard REFUSAL: such an entry is indistinguishable from one that is not there. A PARTIAL merge stays a warning, `operator_compose_partial_merge`, because an operator may legitimately contribute states of its own alongside the ones it does merge and the format cannot tell the two apart. (2) `require_match` is TRI-STATE and absent is NOT `false`: absent means the author has not said (zero-merge refuses); `true` means the systems[1] equations are contributions and ANY shortfall — partial included — is `operator_compose_require_match_unmatched`; `false` is an explicit DECLARATION of a standalone-contributing operator, under which nothing is reported. Each of the three has a non-vacuity anchor here, so a binding cannot pass by being uniformly strict or uniformly lax. (3) A BARE-NAME match that would unify two STATES is `operator_compose_ambiguous_bare_name`, a refusal: each state carries its own initial condition, the merge keeps one, and the document has not said which — deciding it silently is exactly how flipping the `systems` order came to change the answer. Where only ONE side is a state the match is not ambiguous and the STATE owns the quantity, in either argument order; that residual branch is pinned too. Like `override_key_diagnostics`, this category compares DIAGNOSTIC OUTCOMES rather than numbers, so it carries no golden: each binding's own suite asserts its idiomatic warning channel and error type per case. Cases that flatten cleanly additionally pin the surviving state's NAME and DEFAULT, because those two — and nothing else — are what used to change with argument order.

diagnostic_surface._comment: The idiomatic channel each binding reports the one WARNING on, and the idiomatic error each raises for the three refusals. The TYPE and CHANNEL are per-language; the OUTCOME classification and the diagnostic CODE are the cross-binding contract. No binding's `flatten` signature carries a diagnostic slot, so the warning goes to whatever stream that language's callers already watch.

warning_channel.rust: eprintln!("warning: …") — the pushdown_rewrite residual-diagnostic idiom — with the side-effect-free `capture_coupling_diagnostics` counterpart for tests
warning_channel.go: the package-level couplingWarnf hook, defaulting to os.Stderr

require_match_truth_table._comment: The tri-state, as a table. `absent` is a distinct state from `false`, which is why the schema declares no default for the property. Every cell is pinned by a case below.

cases.note: The issue's Symptom 2, verbatim. The operator writes a species the mechanism does not carry, so the entry is indistinguishable from one that is not there: the operator would integrate a private decoupled decay from its own default and the mechanism would receive nothing. Refused at FLATTEN, not at validate: the document is schema-valid and structurally valid, and only the merge knows the answer. Same placement rule as coupling/couple_multiplicative_no_tendency.esm.

NON-VACUITY ANCHOR for the zero-merge refusal, and the escape hatch the nine annotated corpus documents use. Same document as `no_merge`, with the author DECLARING a standalone-contributing operator. Nothing is reported and step 5 preserves the equations. A binding that refused every zero merge unconditionally passes `no_merge` and fails here.

The seven-of-twelve-species shape reduced to one-of-two. `Chem.O3` gains the deposition term; the operator's CO tendency lands nowhere and survives decoupled. A WARNING and not a refusal: unlike a zero merge, a partial merge is indistinguishable from an operator that legitimately contributes states of its own alongside the ones it does merge.

Same document as `no_merge`, with `require_match: true`. It refuses under either state, but with the code that says WHICH: the author declared an intent, so the fix is to correct the names rather than to add the declaration.

THE CASE `require_match: true` EXISTS FOR: a partial merge is only a warning by default, and this is the author saying it must not be. There is no 'some is enough' reading -- an operator that reaches seven of twelve species and silently misses five is the defect the flag catches.
NON-VACUITY ANCHOR for `require_match: true`. Without it, a binding that refused every `require_match` entry would pass both refusals above.

The issue's Symptom 1 document verbatim. Both `Sink.O3` and `Chem.O3` are states with their own defaults, the bare-name fallback binds them on a shared local name alone, and the merge keeps one -- so the choice decides which initial condition the system integrates from. Under the old behaviour this silently produced `Sink.O3` at 40.0.

THE ORDER-INDEPENDENCE PIN. Identical models in identical declaration order; ONLY the `systems` array is reversed. Under the old behaviour this produced `Chem.O3` at 30.0 while its twin produced `Sink.O3` at 40.0 -- an argument order silently choosing an initial condition. Both must now refuse, with the same code.

NON-VACUITY ANCHOR for the ambiguity refusal, and the documented FIX: the same document with a `translate` map naming the surviving spelling. A translation match is the author saying which name the quantity keeps, so nothing is guessed. A binding that refused every bare-name-shaped composition passes both refusals above and fails here.

The UNAMBIGUOUS bare-name match -- the residual case ownership still decides. `Diag.O3` is an observed (a bare-LHS equation defines it) and carries no initial condition; `Sink.O3` is a state and does. Only one IC is at stake, so the state owns the quantity and the observed name is retargeted onto it. Here the observed side is `systems[0]`, so the surviving spelling is NOT `systems[0]`'s -- this is the direction the old rule got wrong.

The flip: the state side is `systems[0]`, so ownership and `systems[0]` agree and the merge is the identity. Same surviving state, same initial condition. The pair is the order-independence pin for the branch that is NOT refused.
